Documentation/Engine

ECS core

Stable Engine Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: ecs/World.hpp

Caffeine uses an archetype-based ECS: entities with the same component set live in contiguous storage, and queries iterate matching archetypes instead of scanning every entity.

Concepts#

Term Meaning
Entity A u32 id plus a World*. No data, no logic, no virtuals.
Component A plain struct registered by type; no methods, no base class.
Archetype The set of entities with an identical ComponentSet; component arrays are contiguous by type.
Query A ComponentQuery describing required, excluded and any-of components.
World Owns entities, archetypes and the component storage.
System An object with onUpdate(World&, f32); the engine or game calls it.

Entity#

cpp
Caffeine::ECS::Entity entity = world.create("Player");

entity.id();        // u32
entity.isValid();   // id != u32_max
entity.add<Position3D>({0, 1, 0});
entity.has<Position3D>();
entity.get<Position3D>();
entity.getOrAdd<Health>(100);
entity.remove<Health>();
entity.destroy();

Entity::INVALID is the default-constructed value. A destroyed entity id may be reused; stale handles are not generation-checked, so treat handles as short-lived and re-query after structural changes.

World#

cpp
Caffeine::ECS::World world;

Entity e = world.create("Cube");
world.add<Transform>(e, Transform{});
world.destroy(e);
world.destroyAll();

world.entityCount();
world.archetypeCount();

auto location = world.getEntityLocation(e);
bool alive = world.isEntityAlive(e);

Queries#

cpp
Caffeine::ECS::ComponentQuery query;
query.with<Position3D, Velocity3D>().without<Disabled>();

world.forEach(query, [](Entity entity, Position3D& position, const Velocity3D& velocity) {
    position.value += velocity.value;
});

ComponentQuery supports:

  • with<T...>() — the archetype must contain every listed component.
  • without<T...>() — the archetype must contain none of them.
  • any<T...>() — at least one of the listed components must be present.
  • matches(const Archetype*) — used by World::forEach.

The callback receives the components requested by the query plus the entity id. The order of arguments follows the query; check the overloads in World.hpp for the exact form.

Parallel iteration#

cpp
world.forEachParallel(query, jobSystem,
    [](Entity entity, Position3D& position, const Velocity3D& velocity) {
        position.value += velocity.value;
    });

forEachParallel splits archetype ranges across the job system. The callback must be safe to run concurrently and must not mutate the world structurally.

Structural changes#

add, remove, destroy and create move entities between archetypes. Do not call them inside forEach / forEachParallel; collect the entities first and apply the changes after iteration. Use CommandBuffer for deferred create/destroy when a system needs to queue structural work.

Systems#

ISystem is intentionally small:

cpp
class ISystem {
public:
    virtual ~ISystem() = default;
    virtual void onUpdate(World& world, f32 deltaTime) = 0;
};

The engine owns the system list (renderer, physics, animation, scripting, game code). There is no hidden global registry; a system is an object the host creates and calls in order. ScriptSystem is one example (src/caffeine/script/ScriptSystem.hpp).

Storage and iteration#

  • Entities are stored in Vector<EntityData>; each entry records the archetype index and the index inside that archetype.
  • Removing an entity swaps the last element into the freed slot; the moved entity's location is patched.
  • Adding/removing a component copies the entity's components into a new archetype, then removes it from the old one.
  • Queries iterate archetypes, so empty archetypes cost almost nothing.

Example: a tiny movement system#

cpp
struct Position3D { Vec3 value; };
struct Velocity3D { Vec3 value; };

World world;
Entity mover = world.create("Mover");
world.add<Position3D>(mover, Position3D{{0, 0, 0}});
world.add<Velocity3D>(mover, Velocity3D{{1, 0, 0}});

ComponentQuery moving;
moving.with<Position3D, Velocity3D>();

world.forEach(moving, [dt](Position3D& position, const Velocity3D& velocity) {
    position.value += velocity.value * dt;
});

Tests#

The ECS suite lives in tests/test_phase2_3.cpp and related files. It covers entity creation/destruction, component add/remove, archetype migration, query matching, parallel iteration and the scene manager integration.
